<s>[INST] Draft a Force Majeure clause for a Master Services Agreement governed by New York, United States law. [/INST] 1. Definition of Force Majeure: For the purposes of this Agreement, "Force Majeure" shall mean any event or circumstance beyond the reasonable control of the affected party, including but not limited to acts of God, natural disasters, pandemics, war, terrorism, cyberattacks, government actions or regulations, strikes, lockouts, or other labor disputes, which prevents or delays the performance of any obligation under this Agreement.

2. Notification Obligation: The party claiming Force Majeure shall provide written notice to the other party within seven (7) days from the date on which such party becomes aware of the Force Majeure event, specifying the nature of the event, the obligations affected, and the anticipated duration of the Force Majeure.

3. Suspension of Obligations: Upon providing the notice as required in sub-clause 2, the obligations of the affected party under this Agreement shall be suspended for the duration of the Force Majeure event, provided that such suspension shall be of no greater scope and no longer duration than is necessary.

4. Duty to Mitigate: The affected party shall use reasonable efforts to mitigate the effects of the Force Majeure event and to resume performance of its obligations under this Agreement as soon as reasonably practicable.

5. Right to Terminate: If the Force Majeure event continues for a period of ninety (90) consecutive days or more, either party shall have the right to terminate this Agreement upon written notice to the other party, without liability, except for obligations that accrued prior to the Force Majeure event.</s>

<s>[INST] Draft a Termination clause for a Employment Agreement governed by Delaware, United States law. [/INST] 1. Termination for Cause: Either party, the Employer or the Employee, may terminate this Agreement for cause upon providing the other party with written notice specifying the nature of the breach. The breaching party shall have a period of 30 days from the receipt of such notice to cure the breach. If the breach is not cured within this period, the non-breaching party may terminate the Agreement immediately upon written notice.

2. Termination for Convenience: The Employer may terminate this Agreement without cause by providing the Employee with 60 days' prior written notice. The Employee may terminate this Agreement without cause by providing the Employer with 30 days' prior written notice.

3. Effects of Termination: Upon termination of this Agreement, the Employee shall return all property, documents, and other materials belonging to the Employer within 10 days. The Employer shall pay the Employee all outstanding compensation and benefits due up to the date of termination within 15 days of the termination date.

4. Survival: The provisions of this Agreement relating to confidentiality, non-disclosure, non-compete, and any indemnification obligations shall survive the termination of this Agreement.</s>
